verdict_text: NO. The merge arithmetic in the loop is sequential rather than both task vectors being taken against the unmodified base: it computes `tmp = b + λ(f1 - b)` and then `tmp + λ(f2 - tmp)`, which expands to `(1-λ)²·b + λ(1-λ)·f1 + λ·f2` = `0.36·b + 0.24·f1 + 0.4·f2`, instead of the required `b + λ(f1-b) + λ(f2-b)` = `0.2·b + 0.4·f1 + 0.4·f2`. This violates "Required result" clause 2 (and is exactly the ordering hazard the spec calls out: the second task vector is taken against a base the first merge already changed). The relative error on all 48 merged tensors far exceeds the 1e-5 Frobenius tolerance in "Grading". Everything else — the shared-tensor verification, the 48/114 count checks, the untouched base tensors, and the single output file — is correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
